table.caption: MAXIMUM BASE HEIGHT AND MAXIMUM BUILDING HEIGHTS FOR QUALIFYING RESIDENTIAL SITES AND QUALIFYING SENIOR HOUSING
columns: Maximum Height of Buildings or other Structures (in feet)
table.table_note: This row is byte-verified to include EVERY R1/R2-series district symbol at 35 ft base / 35 ft building height: R1-1, R1-2, R1-2A, R2, R2A, R2X (plus R3-1/R3-2/R3A/R3X, out of this family's scope - those are M4-T014's R3/R4-series territory). Note bare 'R1' does NOT appear in this table (only R1-1/R1-2/R1-2A do); the R1/R2/R2X QRS rule this snapshot supports is therefore scoped to the six symbols actually named here, never to bare 'R1'.

notes: The 23-424 alternative (taller-than-standard for these districts) envelope - base height 35 ft, building height 35 ft (i.e. NO setback headroom above the base for this row, unlike the R4/R5 rows) - applies ONLY on a 'qualifying residential site' (section 12-10). That geography cannot be evaluated from the canonical property_profile, so the citing rule fails closed to professional_review_required with no value when the qualifying flag is unknown.

This snapshot is INDEPENDENT of the already-accepted M4-T006 zr-23-424 snapshot (which captures only the R5-series row of the SAME table); both are byte-verified against the same official print/PDF artifact and are not in conflict.

Whether a specific lot qualifies is a separate legal determination (section 12-10) NOT decided by this snapshot or any agent; the owner's research additionally flags that the ORDINARY transit-proximity qualifying route excludes R1/R2 (other routes, e.g. a community-facility floor-space condition as of 2024-12-05, can include them) - the citing rule's limitations disclose this nuance rather than assuming either outcome.
